{{short description|Type of Riemannian manifold with constant Jacobi operator spectrum}}
In [[mathematics]], particularly in [[differential geometry]], an '''Osserman manifold''' is a [[Riemannian manifold]] in which the [[characteristic polynomial]] of the [[Jacobi operator]] of [[unit vector|unit]] [[tangent vector]]s is a constant on the unit [[tangent bundle]].<ref>{{cite journal |author=Balázs Csikós and Márton Horváth |year=2011 |title=On the volume of the intersection of two geodesic balls |journal=Differential Geometry and Its Applications}}</ref> It is named after [[Americans|American]] [[mathematician]] [[Robert Osserman]]. 

== Definition ==
Let <math>M^n</math> be a [[Riemannian manifold]]. For a point <math>p \in M^n</math> and a [[unit vector]] <math>X \in T_pM^n</math>, the Jacobi operator <math>R_X</math> is defined by <math>R_X = R(X,\cdot)X</math>, where <math>R</math> is the [[Riemann curvature tensor]].<ref name="Nikolayevsky-2003">{{cite journal |author=Y. Nikolayevsky |year=2003 |title=Two theorems on Osserman manifolds |journal=Differential Geometry and Its Applications |volume=18 |issue=3 |pages=239–253|doi=10.1016/S0926-2245(02)00160-2 |doi-access=free }}</ref> A manifold <math>M^n</math> is called '''pointwise Osserman''' if, for every <math>p \in M^n</math>, the [[Spectrum (functional analysis)|spectrum]] of the [[Jacobi operator]] does not depend on the choice of the unit vector <math>X</math>. The manifold is called '''globally Osserman''' if the spectrum depends neither on <math>X</math> nor on <math>p</math>. All two-point [[homogeneous space]]s are globally Osserman, including [[Euclidean space]]s <math>\mathbb{R}^n</math>, [[real projective space]]s <math>\mathbb{RP}^n</math>, [[sphere]]s <math>\mathbb{S}^n</math>, [[hyperbolic space]]s <math>\mathbb{H}^n</math>, [[complex projective space]]s <math>\mathbb{CP}^n</math>, [[complex hyperbolic space]]s <math>\mathbb{CH}^n</math>, [[quaternionic projective space]]s <math>\mathbb{HP}^n</math>, [[Hyperbolic quaternion|quaternionic hyperbolic space]]s <math>\mathbb{HH}^n</math>, the [[Cayley projective plane]] <math>\mathbb{C}ayP^2</math>, and the [[Cayley plane|Cayley hyperbolic plane]] <math>\mathbb{C}ayH^2</math>.<ref name="Nikolayevsky-2003"/>

== Properties ==
''Clifford structures'' are fundamental in studying Osserman manifolds. An [[Riemann curvature tensor|algebraic curvature tensor]] <math>R</math> in <math>\mathbb{R}^n</math> has a <math>\text{Cliff}(\nu)</math>-structure if it can be expressed as
:<math>R(X,Y)Z = \lambda_0(\langle X,Z \rangle Y - \langle Y,Z \rangle X) + \sum_{i=1}^{\nu} \frac{1}{3}(\lambda_i - \lambda_0)(2\langle J_iX,Y \rangle J_iZ + \langle J_iZ,Y \rangle J_iX - \langle J_iZ,X \rangle J_iY)</math>
where <math>J_i</math> are [[Antisymmetric relation|skew-symmetric]] [[orthogonal]] [[operator (mathematics)|operators]] satisfying the Hurwitz relations <math>J_iJ_j + J_jJ_i = -2\delta_{ij}I</math>.<ref>{{cite journal |author=P. Gilkey, A. Swann, L. Vanhecke |year=1995 |title=Isoparametric geodesic spheres and a conjecture of Osserman concerning the Jacobi operator |journal=[[Quarterly Journal of Mathematics]] |volume=46 |issue=3 |pages=299–320|doi=10.1093/qmath/46.3.299 }}</ref> A Riemannian manifold is said to have <math>\text{Cliff}(\nu)</math>-structure if its curvature tensor also does. These structures naturally arise from unitary representations of [[Clifford algebra]]s and provide a way to construct examples of Osserman manifolds. The study of Osserman manifolds has connections to [[isospectral geometry]], [[Einstein manifold]]s, [[Curvature of Riemannian manifolds#Curvature_operator|curvature operator]]s in differential geometry, and the classification of [[symmetric space]]s.<ref name="Nikolayevsky-2003"/>

== Osserman conjecture ==
{{unsolved|mathematics|Are all Osserman manifolds either [[flat manifold|flat]] or locally rank-one [[symmetric spaces]]?}}
The '''Osserman conjecture''' asks whether every Osserman manifold is either a [[flat manifold]] or locally a rank-one [[symmetric space]].<ref>{{cite journal |author=Y. Nikolayevsky |year=2011 |title=Conformally Osserman manifolds of dimension 16 and a Weyl–Schouten theorem for rank-one symmetric spaces |journal=[[Annali di Matematica Pura ed Applicata]]}}</ref>

Considerable progress has been made on this conjecture, with proofs established for manifolds of dimension <math>n</math> where <math>n</math> is not divisible by 4 or <math>n = 4</math>. For pointwise Osserman manifolds, the conjecture holds in dimensions <math>n \neq 2</math> not divisible by 4. The case of manifolds with exactly two [[eigenvalue]]s of the Jacobi operator has been extensively studied, with the conjecture proven except for specific cases in dimension 16.<ref name="Nikolayevsky-2003"/>
